topics.title: Rule resolution process and Rule availability

elements.description: Rule resolution chooses behavior for a purpose in the current requestor context. A Rule being saved in the database does not make it accessible or the winner. Diagnose the class, runtime Ruleset stack, version, circumstance and availability together.

elements.text: Worked example: A newer Rule that exists only in an inaccessible Ruleset cannot win for this operator. Start with context, not the database’s latest version.

elements.description: Purpose combines Rule name and Rule type. Candidate filtering excludes Not Available instances, inapplicable Rulesets/versions and classes outside the inheritance path. Do not compare version numbers until the candidates are eligible.

elements.text: Worked example: CalculateFee as a Decision Table is not the same purpose as CalculateFee as an Activity. Match both name and type.

elements.description: Ranking considers class, Ruleset, circumstance/date qualifiers and version. An unqualified default provides fallback; lower-ranked candidates below it are discarded. Withdrawal removes matching same-class/purpose instances at or below its version in its Ruleset, while eligible other scopes remain. The cache retains candidates for later selection.

elements.text: Worked example: Two eligible candidates in the same class differ by circumstance and version. A later ordinary base does not automatically erase an older qualifying variant.

elements.title: Rank eligible candidates in this order

elements.description: Check the cache, build candidates on a miss, find the best matching eligible circumstance or default, then check blocking and authorization. Equally correct matches cause a duplicate-Rule error. A candidate being cached does not guarantee it runs.

elements.text: Worked example: If two candidates are equally correct, resolve the ambiguity; do not assume the system selects whichever was saved last.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Rule resolution process and Rule availability

elements.description: Available can run. Final can run but prevents same-name overrides in another Ruleset; a higher version in its own Ruleset is the exception. Not Available is skipped. A selected unqualified Blocked Rule stops execution. Withdrawn suppresses its matching earlier scope and allows other eligible fallback. Circumstanced Blocked/Withdrawn variants are excluded while remaining siblings can be considered.

elements.text: Worked example: For an ordinary Rule: Not Available skips the instance; Blocked halts if selected; Withdrawn removes the defined earlier scope. Inspect qualifiers before applying the ordinary-rule case.

elements.title: Close the notes and explain

elements.text: Try the quiz before rereading. Explain why each distractor fails. Use Smart Review on later days; revisit answers you got wrong with high confidence.

examPitfalls.title: Newest wins
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The highest database version always executes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Filter by context first, then rank and match.

examPitfalls.title: Blocked vs skipped
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Blocked and Not Available both just fall back.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A selected unqualified Blocked Rule halts; Not Available is skipped.

examPitfalls.title: Final nuance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Final prevents any higher version in its own Ruleset.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: It allows the same-Ruleset higher-version exception.

examPitfalls.title: Circumstance nuance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every Blocked variant halts the whole family.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Circumstanced Blocked/Withdrawn instances are excluded while siblings remain eligible.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Decision Table and a Flow Action share the name Review. Do they have the same Rule purpose?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A shared label does not make two different Rule types interchangeable.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Rule filtering by purpose. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The newest Rule exists in a Ruleset absent from the operator’s stack. Does its version guarantee selection?

options.text: No, it is outside the eligible context

practiceQuiz.hint: Start with the current requestor context rather than the database’s latest version.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The highest eligible unqualified instance is Not Available; an older eligible instance remains. What should happen?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Not Available excludes a candidate rather than blocking execution.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Rule resolution process and Rule availability. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A selected unqualified Rule is Blocked. What is the expected result?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blocked is not equivalent to skipping a Not Available candidate.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Rule resolution process and Rule availability. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements distinguish Final from Not Available?

options.text: Not Available prevents all parent-class fallback

practiceQuiz.rationale: Final protects overriding; Not Available removes the instance from execution.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Rule resolution process and Rule availability. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two equally correct best matches remain. What is the expected outcome?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Matching ambiguity is an error rather than a tie-break by name.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on The Rule resolution process. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After matching a candidate, the operator lacks its required authorization. What happens?

options.text: Skip the privilege check if cached

practiceQuiz.rationale: Selection and permission are separate checks.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on The Rule resolution process. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A withdrawn unqualified Rule suppresses its older same-class/purpose instances. Which may still remain eligible?

options.text: A matching Rule in another eligible scope
A Rule of any unrelated type

practiceQuiz.rationale: Withdrawal has scope; inherited or other Ruleset candidates can remain.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Remaining Rule candidates and ranking. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

quickRecap.value: Class → Ruleset → circumstance → circumstance date → date/time range → version.
Final runs; Not Available skips; selected ordinary Blocked halts; Withdrawn suppresses its defined scope.
Matching, ambiguity, blocking and authorization all matter.
Blocked/Withdrawn circumstanced variants are excluded; evaluate remaining siblings.
